summary: Every Thursday or Friday, Michelle Lokay builds the California Capacity Report by hand and sends it to the Transwestern commercial team. It covers Transwestern and El Paso deliveries to California, capacity utilization percentages, posted Gas Daily prices and Enron basis. A scheduled job would collect the week's figures, do the averages and percentages, fill in the week dates in the subject, and leave a ready-to-send draft in the existing layout. That saves roughly 0.9 h/month ($73/month, $876/year) and removes errors from retyping and copying last week's email, such as the wrong-week correction seen in January.

current_workflow.step: At the end of each week (Thursday before a holiday or short week, otherwise Friday), the analyst collects Transwestern's average deliveries to California, San Juan lateral throughput and total East deliveries for the week.

The analyst collects El Paso's average deliveries to California for the PG&ETop, SoCalEhr and SoCalTop delivery points, looks up each point's capacity (SoCalEhr changed from 1042 to 1250 and SoCalTop from 512 to 540 between October and December), and works out each utilization percentage by hand.

The analyst copies the day's posted Gas Daily prices and day-over-day changes for SoCal gas, PG&E, TW San Juan (later 'San Juan (non-Bondad)') and TW Permian, entering 'n/a' when a price is not posted.
The analyst adds Enron Online / Enron basis spreads (Perm-CA, SJ-CA, SJ-Waha, Perm-Waha) while they are available. From late December they read 'n/a', and from February the section is dropped.

The analyst types the subject line 'California Capacity Report for Week of MM/DD-MM/DD' and emails the report to the same fixed list (Steven Harris, Kimberly Watson, Lorraine Lindberg, TK Lohman, Lindy Donoho).
When the week label on a sent report is wrong, the analyst sends a correction to the whole distribution list.

stall_points.description: The report's week label is typed by hand, likely by reusing the previous week's email. A wrong effective date went out and needed a follow-up correction to all five recipients.
stall_points.quote: Sorry, the effective date for this new report is 01/07-01/11.

stall_points.description: The analyst keeps delivery-point capacities in her head or in last week's email. This October figure for SoCalEhr (1042) differs from the 1250 used from December, so each utilization percentage depends on a manually maintained capacity value and a hand calculation.
stall_points.quote: SoCalEhr, capacity 1042 MMBtu/d, deliveries of 707 MMBtu/d (68%)

stall_points.description: El Paso volumes come from a third-party pipeline and are re-averaged and re-typed every week, together with the overall California utilization percentage.
stall_points.quote: El Paso's average deliveries to California were 2198 MMBtu/d (75%):

stall_points.description: Transwestern delivery, San Juan lateral and East figures are re-keyed into the same sentence every week. This is the repetitive core of the roughly 30 minutes of handling per report.
stall_points.quote: Transwestern's average deliveries to California were 1011 MMBtu/d (93%), with San Juan lateral throughput at 872 MMBtu/d.  Total East deliveries averaged 337 MMBtu/d.

solution.approach: A weekly scheduled job runs on the report day. It reads the week's daily Transwestern deliveries to California, San Juan lateral throughput and East deliveries, plus El Paso's daily deliveries at PG&ETop, SoCalEhr and SoCalTop, and averages them over the business days of the reporting week. It divides each average by capacity from a small maintained table of delivery-point capacities, keeps Transwestern's percentage basis, and computes the percentages. It pulls the latest posted Gas Daily prices and the change from the prior posting for the four quoted locations, writing 'n/a' when no price is posted, and adds the Enron Online basis block only when quotes are available. It fills the existing email layout, builds the subject 'California Capacity Report for Week of MM/DD-MM/DD' from the calendar, and saves a draft addressed to the standing distribution list. The analyst checks the numbers, adds any commentary and sends it.
solution.trigger: Weekly schedule on the last business day of the week (Friday, or Thursday when the week is short), early enough for the draft to be ready before the usual mid-morning send.
inputs: Daily Transwestern deliveries to California, San Juan lateral throughput and total East deliveries for the reporting week
Daily El Paso deliveries at PG&ETop, SoCalEhr and SoCalTop for the reporting week
Delivery-point capacity table (PG&ETop, SoCalEhr, SoCalTop, and the Transwestern California capacity used for its percentage)
Posted Gas Daily prices and day-over-day changes for SoCal gas large pkgs, PG&E large pkgs, San Juan (non-Bondad) / TW San Juan, and TW Permian
Enron Online basis quotes for Perm-CA, SJ-CA, SJ-Waha and Perm-Waha, when available
Business-day calendar, used to work out the week range and report day
outputs: Draft email to the analyst in the existing layout, with a calendar-generated subject, ready to review and send
Exception notes at the top of the draft for the analyst: missing source days, a price not posted, a capacity value changed since last week, or a week-over-week swing beyond a threshold
Archived weekly figures (one row per week) so the commercial team can see trends without searching old emails
components: Data extract for Transwestern and El Paso daily delivery volumes (source to be confirmed with the analyst)
Maintained delivery-point capacity table with an effective date for each value
Gas Daily price loader with 'n/a' handling for unposted locations
Email template renderer that reproduces the current report layout and builds the week-range subject
Exception and sanity-check rules (missing days, capacity change, large swings)

implementation_steps: Sit with the analyst for one report cycle to confirm where each figure comes from: Transwestern volumes, El Paso volumes, capacities, Gas Daily prices and the Enron Online basis. Also confirm whether each percentage is computed over business days or calendar days.
Build the capacity table from the most recent reports (PG&ETop 1140, SoCalEhr 1250, SoCalTop 540) with effective dates, and assign an owner to update it.
Write the template renderer to reproduce the current email body and subject exactly, then check it by re-rendering several past weeks from their published figures.
Build the extracts and the Gas Daily loader, and calculate averages and percentages in code.
Run in parallel for three or four weeks: the job produces a draft while the analyst still builds the report by hand, and any differences are reconciled.
Switch to draft-and-review: the job saves the draft, and the analyst reviews, adds commentary and sends.
Add the weekly archive and the exception rules, and review the thresholds with the recipients after one month.
stays_manual: Final review and send: recipients use these numbers for commercial decisions, so a person confirms they are plausible before they go out.
Market commentary or explanation of unusual weeks, which needs judgment.
Updating delivery-point capacities when El Paso or Transwestern capacity changes, because the change is announced outside the data feed.
Deciding whether to include or drop a section (for example, the Enron basis block that went to 'n/a' and was later removed) when the data source is unavailable.
risks: The evidence never names where Transwestern and El Paso volumes come from. If El Paso data is only available from a manual website lookup, automation may need screen-scraping or may stay partly manual. Confirm sources before funding the build.

The value is small, $73/month ($876/year), from a single mailbox over about five active months. A full integration may not pay back. A lighter version (a spreadsheet that calculates percentages and generates the subject from the calendar) captures most of the error reduction for less effort.

Capacity values change: SoCalEhr went from 1042 to 1250 and SoCalTop from 512 to 540. A stale capacity table would silently misstate utilization. Mitigate with effective-dated capacities and a flag whenever a percentage is above 100% (Transwestern reached 103%) or moves sharply.

Gas Daily prices are sometimes not posted for a location ('n/a'), and location names change (TW San Juan to San Juan (non-Bondad)). The loader must handle gaps and renames without carrying forward a stale price.
Report-day changes (Thursday on short weeks) and holiday weeks (12/26-12/28, 02/19-02/22) must come from a business calendar, or the week label will repeat the error behind the January correction.
Gas Daily content licensing may restrict automated extraction. Confirm before building the loader.
success_metric: Share of weekly reports sent without a follow-up correction, together with the analyst's minutes per report (target: review only), tracked over the first 8 weeks after switching to draft-and-review.
